journeys.title: First steps: understanding AI
journeys.description: Start with rules and search. See how examples teach a model, then explore text, tools and checks. Begin with six key words, then follow the steps. Read each plain-language introduction before choosing whether to go deeper.

journeys.title: How modern language systems work
journeys.description: Follow a language application from its architecture and training to external knowledge, tool use and the checks that make its results more useful.

journeys.title: Building trustworthy industrial AI
journeys.description: Connect explicit knowledge, evidence retrieval, constraints and uncertainty. Explore what makes an answer inspectable and when the system should defer.

journeys.title: From prediction to action
journeys.description: Learn how models, policies, planning and simulation work together when an AI system has to choose actions in an environment.

journeys.title: From sensor data to useful alerts
journeys.description: Build a monitoring workflow: estimate hidden states, detect unusual behavior, evaluate rare-event alerts, and decide when to investigate. Connect model quality to operational decisions.

frontiers.title: Reasoning that knows when to check
frontiers.demonstrated: Reasoning-oriented reinforcement learning and reflective planning have shown gains on selected tasks. External feedback can help a system select, revise or reject proposed actions.
frontiers.direction: More selective controllers could spend extra computation on difficult cases, call a verifier, gather evidence or defer when the available checks are insufficient.
frontiers.caution: A model describing its own uncertainty is not the same as a calibrated error estimate. Dependable general self-correction has not been established.

refs.title: Learning from Trials and Errors: Reflective Test-Time Planning for Embodied LLMs

frontiers.title: Memory beyond the prompt
frontiers.demonstrated: Titans investigates learned memory at inference time. Nested Learning explores interacting learning processes and memory at different update frequencies.
frontiers.direction: Future systems may combine temporary context, external records and controlled learned updates, choosing a memory mechanism to suit the information and task.
frontiers.caution: Persistent adaptation also creates persistent mistakes. Forgetting, interference, rollback and the authority to update a model remain important constraints.

refs.title: Nested Learning: The Illusion of Deep Learning Architectures
Titans: Learning to Memorize at Test Time

frontiers.title: Language beyond left-to-right
frontiers.demonstrated: Diffusion language models generate through iterative denoising rather than exclusively choosing the next token. A 2026 experimental study compares generation quality and computational efficiency across several models and tasks.
frontiers.direction: Parallel refinement and flexible editing could create useful alternatives for some generation workloads, alongside autoregressive and hybrid approaches.
frontiers.caution: Fewer sequential generation steps do not automatically mean a faster or cheaper system. Compare actual latency, throughput and quality under matching conditions.

refs.title: Diffusion Language Models: An Experimental Analysis

frontiers.title: Learning to anticipate the world
frontiers.demonstrated: V-JEPA 2 studies self-supervised video representations and action-conditioned prediction for planning. This is one route to world modelling, alongside generative simulation and other dynamics models.
frontiers.direction: Stronger links between learned dynamics, action policies and feedback may allow systems to evaluate possible actions before carrying them out.
frontiers.caution: A plausible predicted future can still be physically wrong. Planning performance depends on model error, coverage of the operating conditions and transfer to reality.

frontiers.title: Neural proposals. Symbolic checks.
frontiers.demonstrated: AlphaGeometry combines a neural language model with symbolic deduction to find geometry proofs. It illustrates a division of work between proposing useful steps and checking formal consequences.
frontiers.direction: Similar combinations may be useful wherever a task can be expressed precisely enough for a solver, checker or trusted rule system to assess candidate outputs.
frontiers.caution: The formal result applies to the encoded problem. Correctly translating messy real-world requirements into that formal representation is a separate challenge.

refs.title: Solving olympiad geometry without human demonstrations
AlphaGeometry: An Olympiad-level AI system for geometry

frontiers.title: Algorithms that evolve
frontiers.demonstrated: AlphaEvolve combines language-model proposals, automated evaluation and evolutionary search to improve candidate programs. The evaluator gives the search a concrete signal about which candidates are worth retaining.
frontiers.direction: More engineering and scientific tasks could use this pattern where candidate outputs can be executed, measured or checked affordably.
frontiers.caution: The system optimizes what its evaluator measures. Weak tests or incomplete objectives can reward brittle solutions, and evaluation itself may be expensive.
